title: Dollar SOARS, Grains SMASHED + Landus Sues Ex-CEO Over $4.4M Salary

bullets: Fed Governor Waller was hawkish. He floated a 50bp hike in December, or clearer guidance on a faster pace of hikes next year
Oct FOMC minutes: broad agreement that more hikes are needed
DXY +0.3% to ~103.87, a 19-month high and the highest close of 2026
USD/BRL: the dollar is up 18.1% since Brazil's runoff election
Pre-market: S&P +1.3%, Nasdaq +2.3%. Jan WTI −0.42 at 81.89
Bloomberg Commodity Index fell more than 2% Wednesday and is −12.8% from its Sep 16 high
Biggest losers: copper −5.3%, silver −4.9%, SRW wheat −4.0%, soy oil −3.7%, gold −3.2%, WTI −2.8%, corn −2.3%
Causes cited: hawkish Fed, strong USD, weaker crude, and year-end/algo speculative liquidation. Nothing specific to grains
Wed: Dec corn −~11¢ to ~4.36, lowest close since late June. Jan beans −~9¢ to ~12.17. Wheat erased Tuesday's gains and more
Thu early: Dec corn unch; Jan beans +4¾ at 12.21½; Dec CBOT wheat +4¼ at 5.74¼; KC +5¾ at 6.15; MGEX +4½ at 6.33¾
Corn's next target is the summer low of 4.25¾. Speculators are selling, and some farmers are being forced to sell grain they can't store
Beans are holding up better. The hosts see excellent demand and a tightening balance sheet
SRW spot month hit its lowest since February. Black Sea peace prospects may be weighing
Trump, Xi and Putin are meeting at APEC on Ukraine and nuclear arms control. No news yet, and the hosts don't expect a peace deal soon
Weekly output 1.13M bpd: +3.2% y/y, a seasonal record
Stocks 24.91M bbl: +12% y/y
Margins are +25–50¢ across the Corn Belt
Wed: live cattle +1.00 to +1.63, feeders +1.43 to +3.50
Landus is suing its ex-CEO Matt Carstens. His base pay allegedly rose from $625K to $4.4M a year, and the co-op wants to claw back his $1.5M severance
Not covered this episode: export-sales numbers, crop progress, South America weather

flags: Auto-captions spell the co-op “Landis” and the CEO “Karsten's”; read as Landus and Carstens
Dec corn this morning is captioned “435 a2”, probably 4.35½
